newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar recovers on Malaysia denial.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar recovers on Malaysia denial.

text.p: The Singapore dollar bounced back in late Asian trade on Thursday as players were heartened by a Malaysian denial of reports Kuala Lumpur had decided to suspend new bilateral ties with Singapore.

After falling to an 18-month low of 1.4528/30 against the U.S. dollar overnight after news reports said the Malaysian cabinet had decided to freeze ties with its neighbour, the Singapore dollar rebounded sharply to 1.4425/35 in late trade.
Dealers said the currency was boosted after lunch by a Malaysian government statement that no decision had been made to freeze ties with Singapore.
"The statements released have been very confusing but it clearly shows there are no thoughts of freezing the ties," said a European bank dealer.

The Malaysian news agency Bernama said late on Wednesday the cabinet had decided to freeze new official dealings, including granting of contracts to Singapore firms, over Singapore elder statesmen Lee Kuan Yew's comment that Malaysia's Johor state was "notorious for shootings, car-jackings and muggings".
Dealers said talk of U.S. dollar sales by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) near the highs of 1.4525/30 in early trade sparked the Singapore dollar's initial recovery.

"Local names were offering good amounts (of U.S. dollars) at 1.4525 this morning and also in London time so it gave the impression that the authority might be behind these offers and made the market very nervous," the dealer said.

He said the amount of dollars sold might not have been substantial, but players were deterred from pushing the U.S. dollar higher by the apparent presence of the de facto central bank, which had not been felt in recent months.

"They haven't come in and stopped the depreciation of the Sing from 1.4100 to the current level. It's the first time the central bank has been rumoured to be in so it really made the market nervous," he said.
He said the Singapore dollar's recovery was also reinforced by stop-loss U.S. dollar sales below the technical support level of 1.4470.
"We're testing another low of 1.4420," he said, adding that a breach of that level could take dollar/Sing back down to 1.4370/75.

"I think people realise that anything above 1.4500 is very dangerous. And most of the funds who've been long dollar/Sing as well as ringgit/Sing would be happy to take profit at those levels," he said.

Dealers said the Singapore dollar was to hit the 1.4500 level in the medium term as it had been under pressure from heavy fund flows into the higher-yielding Malaysian ringgit since the beginning of the year.
The Singapore dollar has depreciated some two percent against the US dollar since the start of the year.
Dealers said talk of intervention by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) helped the Singapore dollar recover from an 18-month low of 1.4525/30 to the U.S. dollar in early trade.
